svg.title: The fly connectome's head-direction ring inside the whole simulated resting brain: a bump of activity in the ellipsoid body holds a heading with no cue and wanders slowly, visiting every heading once each ring neuron has scaled its synapses from outside the ring
svg.text: The connectome's compass, inside the whole resting brain
its EPGs' bump holds a heading with no cue and wanders slowly, like a fly's in darkness
16 wedges, lit by their EPGs' spikes; 40 s at 5× real time
The same run over 120 s: where the bump sits
This run drifts at D = 0.030 rad²/s; flies' bumps in darkness, about 0.003–0.04.
Each: the share of time at each of the 16 wedges over 8 runs of 300 s on fresh seeds;
rung 4 asks an entropy of at least 0.9 and resultants under 0.6.
